title: Event enrichment pipeline and SLI data contract for cost-attribution dashboards
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
The console backend emits high-volume usage events (generation calls, embeddings, reranks) that feed the analytics pipeline. Currently events lack consistent SLI context (tenant journey, latency budget bucket, KV-cache hit flags, model variant) and lineage metadata, which limits our ability to: 1) attribute SLI violations to upstream causes, 2) surface per-tenant cost hotspots in dashboards, and 3) replay traces to validate SLO regressions.

Goal:
Create an event enrichment stage and a lightweight SLI data contract so that every analytics event contains a stable set of fields for SLO/SLA computation, cost attribution, and trace linkage. Deliver dashboards that show: per-tenant latency SLO attainment, cost per effective token by journey, and heatmaps correlating KV cache misses with tail latency. Provide a rollout plan that is low-risk and reversible.

Scope (in-scope):
- Define a minimal SLI data contract (schema v1) for console->analytics events (tenant_id, journey, route_id, model_variant, seq_len_bucket, latency_ms, kv_cache_hit, token_count, request_id, parent_trace_id, env).
- Implement an enrichment service in the console backend close to the request boundary that attaches derived fields (journey, seq_len_bucket, latency_ms, kv_cache_hit).
- Produce enriched events to the existing Kafka topic analytics.events.enriched with schema registry validation.
- Backfill a short window (48h) of enriched events for comparative dashboards during rollout.
- Build dashboards in Grafana/Looker showing SLI attainment, cost-attribution by journey, and KV cache miss correlation.
- Add synthetic probe that exercises slow-paths to validate SLOs post-rollout.

Out of scope:
- Full per-token billing reconciliation (separate billing pipeline).
- Long-term archival/retention changes beyond default analytics retention.

Design decisions and rationale:
1) Minimal contract: limit high-cardinality fields (avoid including free-form user prompt hashes) to keep downstream cost manageable. We will use controlled enums for journey and model_variant.
2) Enrichment location: do enrichment in console backend to have immediate access to request context (tenant, route, auth) and avoid unreliable joins in the pipeline. This keeps event payloads small and deterministic.
3) Kafka topic + Schema Registry: use Avro/Protobuf schema in registry to enable strict validation and smoother migrations.
4) KV cache indicator: emit a simple boolean and a small cause enum (e.g., cold_miss, seq_mismatch, eviction) for rich debugging but not for billing.

Data contract (high-level v1 fields):
- tenant_id (string)
- env (enum: prod|staging|canary)
- route_id (string)
- journey (enum: chat|completion|embedding|rerank)
- model_variant (enum: gptx-16k, gptx-32k, llama-q8)
- seq_len_bucket (enum: <128|128-512|512-2048|>2048)
- latency_ms (integer)
- token_count (integer)
- kv_cache_hit (boolean)
- kv_cache_cause (enum|null)
- request_id (string)
- parent_trace_id (string|null)
- generated_at (ISO8601)

Trade-offs considered:
- Cardinatlity vs observability: we deliberately avoid shipping raw prompt metadata to the pipeline to contain storage/query costs. If this prevents a future root-cause, we'll introduce sampled debug-mode events behind a tenant opt-in.
- Enrichment CPU cost: performing enrichment at request time will add CPU; we measured rough 0.5-2ms per request in a microbenchmark. Acceptable for SLOs but needs capacity consideration for peak.

Implementation plan (milestones):
1) Schema and contract doc (PRD + Confluence) - owner: Asha (target 2026-03-11)
2) Console enrichment library + config flag (non-prod) - owner: Michael (2026-03-14)
3) Schema Registry registration + CI checks - owner: infra-api (2026-03-14)
4) Consumers update (analytics ingestion service) to accept enriched events - owner: analytics-team (2026-03-16)
5) Backfill job and compare dashboards - owner: data-eng (2026-03-17)
6) Canary release in prod for 10% traffic + synthetic probe - owner: Michael (2026-03-18)
7) Full rollout and dashboard promotion - owner: product-obs (2026-03-20)

Acceptance criteria:
- 95% of console events in prod contain the full v1 SLI contract for three consecutive days.
- Dashboards show clear per-tenant SLI attainment and a cost-per-journey metric computed from enriched fields.
- Synthetic probe reproduces a KV cache cold miss and the event appears enriched end-to-end with parent_trace_id linking to a trace in our tracing system.
- No significant increase (>5%) in p95 request latency for console control-plane operations after enabling enrichment for 10% canary.

Monitoring and alerts:
- Alert: daily % of events missing v1 fields > 2% -> pager to analytics-oncall.
- Alert: canary p95 increase >5% -> automated rollback of enrichment flag for that shard.
- SLOs defined: journey-level latency SLOs (p95 < 120ms for embeddings route in prod) and p99 budget alerts for specific tenant tiers.

Rollout and rollback strategy:
- Feature flag gated per-shard and per-region. Start with staging -> one prod shard at 10% traffic -> evaluate backfill comparisons and probe results -> 50% -> 100%.
- If canary p95 latency or event schema validation errors spike, auto-disable enrichment and notify oncall with runbook link.

Security and privacy notes:
- Enrichment must not include user prompt content or any PII. Schema registry will enforce field whitelist.
- Security review flagged as required: KMS access for signing events and schema ACLs must be validated (security_review_required=true).

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for enrichment library and schema validation.
- Integration test: produce enriched event to test Kafka topic and validate consumer acceptance.
- End-to-end canary with synthetic probe that asserts trace linkage.

Docs and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Event+Enrichment+and+SLI+Contract+v1
- Schema Registry PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/schemas/pull/342
- Console feature branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1892
- Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/analytics/sli-cost-attribution

Acceptance test checklist (manual):
- [ ] Schema v1 deployed to registry and consumers updated.
- [ ] Console enrichment flag enabled for staging and validated.
- [ ] Backfill comparison job results show near-identical SLI computations between enriched and baseline for last 48h.
- [ ] Synthetic probe trace visible in tracing UI and linked from dashboard.
- [ ] Security review completed and signed off.

Notes and open questions:
- Q: Should we include a sampled debug event with raw prompt hash for tenants who opt-in? A: Defer to follow-up ticket; mark as privacy impact.
- Q: How do we attribute cost for multi-route composite requests? A: For now attribute by primary route_id; follow-up work required for composite attribution.
